Ch 8 · Introduction to Trigonometry — Practice

Attempt first, then open the answer. Everything here is original practice material mapped to the current syllabus.

MCQs

The value of cos 60° is: (a) 1/2 (b) √3/2 (c) 1/√2 (d) 1

(a) 1/2.

sin²30° + cos²30° equals: (a) 0 (b) 1/2 (c) 1 (d) 3/4

(c) 1. That is the fundamental identity.

tan 45° × cot 45° is: (a) 0 (b) 1 (c) 2 (d) undefined

(b) 1. tan and cot are reciprocals.

Written questions

1 marks Evaluate sin 60° cos 30° + cos 60° sin 30°.

(√3/2)(√3/2) + (1/2)(1/2) = 3/4 + 1/4 = 1.

2 marks If sin A = 3/5, find cos A and tan A (A is acute).

Draw the right triangle: opposite = 3, hypotenuse = 5, so adjacent = √(25 − 9) = 4.
cos A = 4/5 and tan A = 3/4.

3 marks Prove that (1 + tan²A)/(1 + cot²A) = tan²A.

Start from the left-hand side.
1 + tan²A = sec²A and 1 + cot²A = cosec²A.
So LHS = sec²A / cosec²A = (1/cos²A) ÷ (1/sin²A) = sin²A/cos²A = tan²A = RHS.

3 marks If tan(A + B) = √3 and tan(A − B) = 1/√3, with 0° < A + B ≤ 90° and A > B, find A and B.

tan(A + B) = √3 gives A + B = 60°.
tan(A − B) = 1/√3 gives A − B = 30°.
Adding: 2A = 90°, so A = 45° and B = 15°.
